gap: No result ChatGPT got says that the two '40 W' lasers make the same one-pass claim (15 mm basswood plywood) but differ on everything else. Snapmaker gives its Artisan 40 W spot as 0.1 × 0.15 mm (0.015 mm²) and Bambu gives the H2D 40 W spot as 0.14 × 0.2 mm (0.028 mm²), so the Artisan has about 1.9× the stated power per mm² and 2.06× the laser bed (400 × 400 vs 310 × 250 mm). At 10 W it reverses: the H2D's 0.0042 mm² spot is 2.4× denser than the Artisan's 0.01 mm². Also, the $1,799 base Artisan ships the 10 W module, not the 40 W.
standout_why: I read four of the pages ChatGPT got. desktop3dprinters.us/topics/3d-printer-laser-combos (cited) gives wattages, work areas and laser class but no spot sizes, and never says whether the watts are optical. desktop3dprinters.us/lists/3d-printers-with-laser-engraver (rank 1, not cited) gives Bambu's spot sizes and the Artisan's 400 × 400 mm area but says outright that it has no Snapmaker spot size, so it can't compare them. 3dengr.com (cited) gives only '10W or 40W diode', with no spot, area or cut depth. engraverpicker.com gives the H2D 15 mm cut and work areas but never mentions the Artisan. None of them puts spot area, power per mm², cut claim and bed area side by side, and none notes that neither maker says whether the rating is optical output. I could not open the Tom's Hardware review or the TechRadar page: Tom's returned only the title and I did not try TechRadar.
decides: It sharpens the split ChatGPT already made. If you mostly laser-cut, or work on big sheets, the Artisan Premium (or a base Artisan plus the $429 40 W module) gives the larger bed and the tighter stated 40 W spot for the same claimed 15 mm cut. At 10 W, the H2D's stated spot is the tighter one, which favours the H2D for fine engraving alongside its better printing. Because neither maker says whether its watts are optical output, '40 W vs 40 W' can't be taken as equal cutting power. It also corrects ChatGPT's table, which shows 'Snapmaker Artisan: 10W / 40W' as if both come in the box: the base Artisan ships 10 W, and 40 W is the Premium or an add-on.
